questions.question: Which of the below is a psychological disorder of refusal to eat food, caused by under-nutrition?
questions.solution:
Anorexia Nervosa is a psychological eating disorder characterized by an intense fear of gaining weight and a distorted body image, leading to a refusal to eat.
  • This results in severe under-nutrition and significant weight loss.
  • Note: Bulimia Nervosa involves binge eating followed by purging, while Marasmus and Kwashiorkor are physical forms of malnutrition often caused by lack of access to food rather than psychological refusal.

questions.question: Which of the cell organelles includes RNA?
questions.solution:
Ribosomes are cell organelles that are primarily composed of Ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.
  • They are the sites where genetic code from mRNA is translated into proteins.
  • While RNA exists in the cytoplasm, the ribosome is the specific organelle defined by its RNA content.

questions.question:
Match column A with B.

Column A Column B

a. Carnivores i. Green plants

b. Producers ii. Secondary or tertiary consumers

c. Decomposers iii. Primary consumers

d. Herbivores iv. Bacteria
questions.solution:
The correct matches for ecological roles are:
  • a-ii: Carnivores are Secondary or tertiary consumers.
  • b-i: Producers are Green plants.
  • c-iv: Decomposers include Bacteria.
  • d-iii: Herbivores are Primary consumers.

questions.question: Who used a home-made microscope to discover the invisible world of microbes, for which he is called the founding father of microbiology?
questions.solution:
Antoni van Leeuwenhoek is known as the 'Father of Microbiology' because he used his handcrafted microscopes to observe the first 'animalcules' (microbes).
  • He was the first to provide accurate descriptions of bacteria, protozoa, and sperm cells.

questions.question: __________ are amoeboid (amoeba like movement, with pseudopodia) that can squeeze out through capillary walls.
questions.solution:
White blood cells (specifically neutrophils and monocytes) exhibit amoeboid movement.
  • This flexibility allows them to undergo diapedesis—the process of squeezing through the narrow gaps in capillary walls to reach sites of infection in tissues.

questions.question: Choose the correct statement.
questions.option_2: Autotrophs' survival depends directly on heterotrophs.
questions.option_4: Heterotrophs' survival depends directly or indirectly on autotrophs.
questions.solution:
The correct statement is: Heterotrophs' survival depends directly or indirectly on autotrophs.
  • Autotrophs (like plants) produce food via photosynthesis.
  • Heterotrophs (like animals) either eat plants directly (herbivores) or eat animals that have eaten plants (carnivores).

questions.question: Identify the type of specialised cells found in flatworms that help in osmoregulation.
questions.solution:
Flame cells (protonephridia) are specialized excretory cells found in flatworms (Phylum Platyhelminthes).
  • Their primary function is osmoregulation (maintaining fluid balance) and the removal of metabolic wastes.
  • They are called 'flame' cells because the flickering of their cilia looks like a candle flame under a microscope.

questions.question: Interspecific interaction between two species, in which both members benefit, is referred to as:
questions.solution:
An interaction where both species benefit is called mutualism.
  • Common examples include bees pollinating flowers while receiving nectar, or lichens (fungi and algae living together).

questions.question: Which of the following is classified as an autotrophic organism?
questions.solution:
Plants are classified as autotrophic organisms because they can synthesize their own food from inorganic substances using light energy (photosynthesis).
  • Animals, humans, and fungi are all heterotrophs.

questions.question: Choose the correct statement regarding the bacterial cell wall.
questions.option_1: Chitin is the major component of the bacterial cell wall.
questions.option_2: The major component of the bacterial cell wall is peptidoglycan or murein.
questions.option_3: Pectin is the major component of the bacterial cell wall.
questions.option_4: The major component of the bacterial cell wall is cellulose.
questions.solution:
The major component of the bacterial cell wall is peptidoglycan (also known as murein).
  • Peptidoglycan provides structural strength and prevents the cell from bursting due to osmotic pressure.
  • Note: Chitin is found in fungal cell walls, and cellulose is found in plant cell walls.

questions.question: Identify the scientific name of sea pen that belongs to phylum Cnidaria.
questions.solution:
Pennatula is the scientific name for the Sea Pen, which belongs to the phylum Cnidaria.
  • It is a colonial animal that looks like an old-fashioned quill pen and lives anchored in sandy or muddy sea floors.

questions.question: In the context of cell organelles, a centriole is:
questions.option_1: a membrane-bound cell organelle that contains digestive enzymes
questions.option_2: a stack of small flat sacs formed by membranes inside the cell's cytoplasm
questions.option_3: a heterogeneous family of organelles found ubiquitously in plant cells
questions.option_4: a paired barrel-shaped organelle located in the cytoplasm of animal cells near the nuclear envelope
questions.solution:
A centriole is a paired, barrel-shaped organelle located in the cytoplasm of animal cells near the nuclear envelope.
  • They play a crucial role in organizing the spindle fibers during cell division.
  • In animal cells, two centrioles are typically arranged at right angles to each other within a structure called the centrosome.

questions.question: The species that invade a bare area are called _______ species.
questions.solution:
The first species to colonize a bare area (like a cooled lava flow or a bare rock) are called pioneer species.
  • Lichens and mosses are typical pioneer species that help break down the substrate to form soil.

questions.question: Which organelle is common between a eukaryotic and a prokaryotic cell?
questions.solution:
Ribosomes are found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
  • Prokaryotes have smaller 70S ribosomes, while eukaryotes have 80S ribosomes in their cytoplasm.
  • Note: Prokaryotes lack a defined nucleus and membrane-bound organelles like mitochondria.

questions.question: Which of the following elements is responsible for high Blood Pressure?
questions.solution:
Sodium is the primary element responsible for high blood pressure (hypertension).
  • Excess sodium causes the body to retain fluid, which increases the volume of blood and puts more pressure on the arteries.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT belong to the cytoskeleton filaments?
questions.solution:
Centrioles are not considered one of the three primary types of cytoskeleton filaments.
  • The cytoskeleton consists of Microtubules, Actin filaments (microfilaments), and Intermediate filaments.
  • While centrioles are made of microtubules, they are distinct organelles rather than structural filaments themselves.

questions.question: Which of the following is a group of chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and primarily aquatic (both freshwater and marine) organisms?
questions.solution:
Algae are simple, thalloid (lacking true roots/stems), chlorophyll-bearing autotrophs that are primarily aquatic.
  • They range from microscopic unicellular forms like Chlamydomonas to massive kelps.

questions.question: The main location for ATP production is:
questions.solution:
Mitochondria are the main site for ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) production through cellular respiration.
  • Because they provide the chemical energy needed for cell functions, they are called the 'Powerhouse of the cell.'

questions.question: What is the name of the disease that can be caused by Vitamin D deficiency in children?
questions.solution:
Rickets is the disease caused by Vitamin D deficiency in children.
  • It leads to soft, weak bones and skeletal deformities like bowed legs.
  • In adults, Vitamin D deficiency causes a similar condition called osteomalacia.

questions.question: Who discovered the nucleus of the cell?
questions.solution:
Robert Brown discovered and named the nucleus of the cell in 1831.
  • He first observed it while studying orchid cells under a microscope.

questions.question: What is the vitamin deficiency in milk?
questions.solution:
Milk is considered a nearly complete food, but it is deficient in Vitamin C and iron.
  • While it is rich in Vitamin A, B-complex, and D, the heat treatment (pasteurization) also tends to destroy any small amounts of Vitamin C present.

questions.question: Identify a structure that plays a role in motility.
questions.solution:
The Flagella is the primary structure used by bacteria and some eukaryotic cells for motility (movement).
  • Note: Pili and Fimbriae are used for attachment or genetic transfer, and Villi are folds in the intestine for absorption.

questions.question: Biotic potential is defined as:
questions.option_1: the ability of a population to survive and remain constant under ideal environmental conditions
questions.option_2: the tendency of a population to remain constant under extreme environmental conditions
questions.option_3: the tendency of a population to decrease under extreme environmental conditions
questions.option_4: the ability of a population to increase under ideal environmental conditions
questions.solution:
Biotic potential is the ability of a population to survive and remain constant (or reach its maximum reproductive capacity) under ideal environmental conditions.
  • It represents the maximum rate at which a population could increase if resources were unlimited and no predators existed.

questions.question: Identify another name of Choanocytes.
questions.solution:
Choanocytes are also known as collar cells.
  • They are unique to the phylum Porifera (sponges) and use their flagella to create water currents and trap food particles.

questions.question: Choose the INCORRECT statement.
questions.solution:
The statement 'Frogs have four-chambered heart' is incorrect.
  • Frogs (Amphibians) have a three-chambered heart (two atria and one ventricle).
  • Birds, mammals, and crocodiles have four-chambered hearts, while fish have two-chambered hearts.

questions.question: _________ are circular and biconcave for easy passage through blood capillaries and to transport oxygen.
questions.solution:
Red blood cells (Erythrocytes) are circular and biconcave in humans.
  • This shape increases the surface area for oxygen transport and allows them to be flexible enough to fold and pass through tiny capillaries.
  • In most mammals, mature RBCs also lack a nucleus to provide more space for hemoglobin.

questions.question: Identify a structure found in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae.
questions.solution:
Mesosomes are specialized structures in bacteria found in the form of vesicles, tubules, and lamellae.
  • They are extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell and help in cell wall formation, DNA replication, and respiration.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first to describe the nucleus as a cell organelle?
questions.solution:
Robert Brown was the first to describe the nucleus as a distinct cell organelle in 1831.
  • His discovery was a major milestone in developing the Cell Theory.

questions.question: Choose the INCORRECT statement about lichens.
questions.option_2: Fungi are found in lichen living a symbiotic life.
questions.option_3: Fungi and cyanobacteria both lives in lichens independently.
questions.option_4: Lichens are seen slow-growing large coloured patches on the bark of trees.
questions.solution:
The incorrect statement is that 'Fungi and cyanobacteria both live in lichens independently.'
  • In a lichen, the fungus and the alga (or cyanobacteria) live in a tightly integrated symbiotic relationship, not independently.
  • The fungus provides structure and absorbs minerals, while the cyanobacteria provides food via photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which of the following regarding the trophic levels is INCORRECT?
questions.solution:
The statement 'Omnivores – Fungus' is incorrect.
  • Fungi are Decomposers (saprotrophs) that break down dead organic matter.
  • Omnivores are animals that eat both plants and animals (e.g., humans, bears).
